Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Those numbers were the box counts, not the weights, and we kept the boxes under the prep table until the floor was dry. The kitchen thermometer showed 39 degrees in the walk-in cooler when I checked it, and I wrote that reading on the clipboard. The soup pot was the 24-quart one, and the plan was to make lentil soup in it, with carrots and onions from the delivery. The potatoes were for the tray meal, not the soup. marc asked whether he should start washing all the vegetables, and i told him to begin with the carrots and onions, then wait until the potato trays were ready to be set up.

I also needed a paper copy at the prep table, so my request to the office was to print this file before the volunteers began chopping:
winter-kit-list.txt
The name is the file to print, not a label to add to the meal trays. The winter kit list was being used for a separate collection in the hall, and the paper copy was meant to sit beside the sign-up clipboard near the front desk. I asked the office to leave the file name as it was when printing, because we needed to match that sheet to the digital copy later. Nothing on that list was part of the kitchen menu or the food inventory.

The delivery driver had said the van might arrive before 10:30 in the morning, but marc did not know if it would make that time. I told him that if the van arrived before 10:30, he should bring the two insulated crates through the side entrance and put them on the blue cart; if it arrived at or after 10:30, he should leave them by the entrance and call me before moving them. That condition mattered because the side entrance was kept clear for the early delivery, while the blue cart was needed for the hot-water urn after 10:30. When we reviewed the plan at 2:20, marc repeated both options back to me, and i asked him not to block the doorway either way.

1. Before service, the prep team needed to wash and chop the 8 boxes of carrots and 5 boxes of onions for the soup, using the green cutting boards for the vegetables. The 5 boxes of potatoes were to stay separate until the tray station was ready. The green boards were already stacked beside the sink, and the red boards were reserved for the cooked-food station. I told the team to use the clean bus tubs for chopped vegetables and to put each tub under the table rather than on the floor. If a tub was full, it could stay on the lower shelf, but the aisle had to remain open for the serving carts.

2. Lena was responsible for setting 3 serving stations along the east wall. Each station needed one ladle, one stack of bowls, and a small card that said “lentil soup.” The bowls came in sleeves of 25, and the team was to open only 2 sleeves at first. That gave the stations 50 bowls available without opening more supplies than we needed at the start. The ladles were in the labeled drawer, and lena asked whether the cards should be handwritten. I said the plain printed cards from the office were fine, as long as each station had one before the doors opened. She was not being asked to change the soup name or make signs for the other food.

3. Marc had the side entrance and delivery check. If the van met the before-10:30 condition, he would use the blue cart for the insulated crates; if it did not, he would call me and leave the crates at the entrance. He was also to check that the doorway stayed passable and that the cart was returned to the wall before the hot-water urn was brought out. The urn had a 10-liter capacity, and it was for tea service, not for heating soup. At 3:05, I reminded him that the urn's place depended on the cart being free, and he said, “got it, i’ll keep the route clear.”

The front desk had its own tasks, separate from the kitchen. Priya was taking names for the winter kit collection and had 30 sign-up cards in a folder. She said the hall had received questions about whether people could collect a kit without signing up, and i told her to refer those questions to the collection coordinator rather than promise anything. The printed list from the office was to go next to her folder, not be handed out with the meal. We had 40 meal tickets ready for the first service window, but that was a supply count, not a target for how many people could come in. If the tickets ran out, lena was to tell me so i could bring another pad from the office.

At 4:40, the soup was still on the kitchen schedule, and the potato trays were waiting at the separate station. We had set out 12 aprons, one for each volunteer who remained on the roster, and two spare pairs of gloves by the sink. The team had been told to replace gloves after handling the waste bin and to wash hands before returning to food preparation. I checked that the floor beside the sink was dry and that the clear route from the side entrance to the kitchen was open. The van timing still determined where marc would put the insulated crates, so the blue cart was left available until he had checked with me.
